os_version: Windows 11 Pro 26100 (measurement over the campaign's saved views)
app: Distiller dedupe pass (DEEPENING-PLAN P2 cross-cutting): closing the XAML dual-role inflation, measured before/after on 9 real app views
channel_setup: uia_probe.dedupe_view: (1) drop lines whose (box,name) exactly duplicate an earlier line (menuitem+button dual roles, doubled address-bar edits); (2) drop text lines whose name equals an enclosing control's name and whose box is contained in it (redundant caption children). Conservative — only true duplicates, no merging.

t1_read_text.detail: No content lost: every dropped line is an exact (box,name) duplicate or a caption child repeating its parent control's name in-place.

t2_enumerate.detail: Interactive enumeration unchanged (controls keep priority; only their echo lines drop).

measurements.notes: Aggregate over 9 saved views: 9151 -> 8637 tokens, 5.6% clawback overall — and the distribution is the finding: the savings concentrate exactly where the duplication lives. Chromium-UIA 16.9% (aria dual-exposure), WPF 12.3%, Notepad/WinUI 10.6% (confirming the ~10% estimate from round 1), Explorer 8.8%, Paint 5.9%; near-zero on Qt (0.7%), JUCE (0.4%), Win32 (2.9%) which don't dual-publish. Per-app: notepad 502->449, explorer 1470->1341, chrome-uia 969->805, wpf 130->114, paint 1901->1788, calculator 666->652. Free lunch: pure post-pass, no extra API calls.

runtime_verification.method: line-level audit of dropped lines on notepad/explorer (each dropped line matched to its surviving twin)
runtime_verification.agreement: all drops are duplicates; deduped views answer the same questions
